item.title: The double standards of a failed execution
item.description:
Christa Pike was supposed to die Wednesday night. Instead, the Tennessee death row inmate reportedly laughed, sang a Buddhist meditation, and eventually snored so loudly that one witness compared it to someone having “the best sleep of her life,” all after prison officials administered two rounds of lethal injection drugs. Pike, 50, was scheduled to be executed at the Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville for the 1995 torture and murder of her classmate, Colleen Slemmer. She would have been the first woman executed by Tennessee in more than 200 years. But the execution was botched. WVLT anchor and senior reporter William Puckett, one of the media witnesses inside the prison, described a surreal scene to the Daily Mail .
